claim_reviews.subject: Final relation and false-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both answers accurately express sudden surprise. The relation is valid as a common-word preference: Indonesian commonly uses kaget, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses terkejut, though both forms can occur across varieties. No false-friend issue is present.

claim_reviews.subject: Final relation and false-friend contrast

response.rationale: Bingung and keliru both express inability to understand or decide clearly. Bingung is characteristic in Indonesian, while keliru is characteristic in Malaysian Malay; bingung is also understood in Malaysian Malay, so the relation is appropriately treated as a common-word preference rather than an exclusive distinction. No false-friend issue is present.
